description:
From the fz-kdt.106 cold review (2026-09-01). ACTIVATION_INPUT_ROW_BUDGET
firing is the primary signal that the compiler is doing history-driven
rather than input-driven work, and after fz-kdt.106 lands a fire means
GENUINE correlation width. Today it is observable only by patching in an
eprintln. Emit a telemetry event carrying the activation key, the row
count at collapse, and the joined projection, so the kdt.106 acceptance
gate (0 collapses corpus-wide) and the compile-work ratchet
(fz-kdt.113-class) can be asserted from telemetry per the
tests-observe-telemetry rule. Baseline at 1d44ac7cd: 3 of 449 dumping
fixtures collapse at base (00420_enum_take_drop_split at 30,
behavior/enum_take_drop_split at 30, behavior/enum_predicate_search at
28); zero after dominance absorption. NOTE: fz-kdt.106's build may land
this in-story since its acceptance depends on it -- if so, close this as
absorbed by that commit.
title: The activation-input row budget needs a telemetry event: a collapse is the history-vs-input work signal
